source.text: Ἔλεγον οὖν τινες ἐκ τῶν Ἱεροσολυμιτῶν· Οὐχ οὗτός ἐστιν ὃν ζητοῦσιν ἀποκτεῖναι;

records.literal_gloss: Were saying therefore some of the Jerusalemites, "Not this [one] is whom they are seeking to kill?

en.L: So some of the people of Jerusalem were saying, "Is this not [the one] whom they are seeking to kill?
en.B: So some who lived in Jerusalem were saying, "Is this not the one they are out to kill?
en.R: Some people from Jerusalem itself said, "Is this not the man our leaders want to kill?

es.L: Decían, pues, algunos de los de Jerusalén: «¿No es este al que buscan matar?
es.B: Entonces algunos de los que vivían en Jerusalén decían: «¿No es este el que quieren matar?
es.R: Algunos que eran de la misma Jerusalén decían: «¿No es este el hombre al que nuestros dirigentes quieren matar?

sw.L: Basi baadhi ya watu wa Yerusalemu walikuwa wakisema, "Je, huyu si [yule] wanayetafuta kumwua?
sw.B: Basi baadhi ya wakazi wa Yerusalemu walikuwa wakisema, "Je, huyu si yule wanayetaka kumwua?
sw.R: Baadhi ya watu wa Yerusalemu kwenyewe wakasema, "Je, huyu si yule mtu ambaye viongozi wetu wanataka kumwua?

decisions.choice: the people of Jerusalem: those who live in the city, not the festival crowd
decisions.reason: John uses a word for the city's own residents, not the crowd of pilgrims at the festival. In 7:20 the crowd denied that anyone wanted to kill Jesus; these local people know better. What the authorities intend (5:18; 7:1, 19) is known in Jerusalem itself.

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer yes
decisions.reason: The question begins with the negative that looks for agreement: "This is the man, is it not?" The speakers are sure of who he is; what puzzles them is what follows in 7:26.

decisions.choice: they: the authorities who have been trying to kill him
decisions.reason: The verb has no named subject. The people speak of the leaders as a group apart from themselves, the same people whose plan John has reported at 5:18 and 7:1.

decisions.choice: the one (B); the man, our leaders (R)
decisions.reason: Literal brackets the word English needs after "this". Readable names who "they" are, as meaning decision m3 explains; the speakers themselves know who wants Jesus dead. Balanced says "out to kill" for a plan already under way.

decisions.choice: nuestros dirigentes
decisions.reason: As in English: Readable names who "they" are (meaning decision m3). Spanish needs no bracket for "al que".

source.text: καὶ ἴδε παρρησίᾳ λαλεῖ καὶ οὐδὲν αὐτῷ λέγουσιν· μήποτε ἀληθῶς ἔγνωσαν οἱ ἄρχοντες ὅτι οὗτός ἐστιν ὁ χριστός;

records.literal_gloss: And look, openly he speaks, and nothing to him they say. Perhaps truly have known the rulers that this is the Christ?

en.L: And look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is speaking openly, and they say nothing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Can it be that the rulers have truly come to know that this is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?
en.B: Look, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is speaking in the open, and they say nothing to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}! Can it be that our leaders really know that this man is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?
en.R: But look! He is speaking out where everyone can hear {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and nobody says anything to {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Is it possible that the leaders really have found out that this man is the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}?

es.L: Y {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}, habla abiertamente, y no le dicen nada. ¿Será que los gobernantes han reconocido de verdad que este es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?
es.B: ¡{{plural_you:Miren|Mirad}}, está hablando en público y no le dicen nada! ¿Será que nuestros dirigentes de verdad saben que este hombre es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?
es.R: ¡Pero {{plural_you:miren|mirad}}! Está hablando donde todos lo pueden oír, y nadie le dice nada. ¿Será posible que los dirigentes de verdad se hayan dado cuenta de que este hombre es el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}?

sw.L: Na tazama, anazungumza waziwazi, wala hawamwambii neno. Je, yawezekana kwamba wakuu wamejua kweli kwamba huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?
sw.B: Tazama, anazungumza hadharani, wala hawamwambii chochote! Je, yawezekana viongozi wetu wanajua kweli kwamba mtu huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?
sw.R: Lakini tazama! Anazungumza mahali ambapo kila mtu anaweza kumsikia, wala hakuna anayemwambia chochote. Je, inawezekana viongozi wamegundua kweli kwamba mtu huyu ndiye {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}?

decisions.choice: openly: in public, plainly, without fear
decisions.reason: The word means speaking freely and in the open. It picks up a thread in this chapter: his brothers urged him to show himself openly (7:4), and no one spoke openly about him for fear of the authorities (7:13). Now Jesus himself does what others fear to do.

decisions.choice: a doubtful question: surely the rulers have not come to know this?
decisions.reason: The word that opens the question puts forward something the speakers hardly believe: "Can it be that...?" They are not saying the rulers accept Jesus. They are puzzled that men who want him dead let him speak, and wonder aloud if the rulers have changed their minds. 7:27 shows that they themselves reject the idea.

decisions.choice: the rulers: the leading members of the Jerusalem council
decisions.reason: The same word is used for Nicodemus, "a ruler of the Jews" (3:1), and in 7:48 the Pharisees ask whether any of the rulers has believed in him. They are the men with authority over the temple and the city.

decisions.choice: the Christ: the Messiah, the anointed king God had promised
decisions.reason: With the article the word is a title, not a name: the one God would anoint to rule, whom the people expected (1:20, 41; 4:25). The question is whether Jesus is that person.

decisions.choice: {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}, {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, {{deity_pronoun:my|My}}, {{deity_pronoun:you|You}}
decisions.reason: Every pronoun for Christ or for God uses the deity_pronoun setting, including "me" and "my" when Jesus speaks of himself, and pronouns for the expected Christ, since John means Jesus (4:25). At the start of a sentence "He" or "My" is written plain. This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}
decisions.reason: Where the Greek has "the Christ" as a title, every level writes "the" before the setting, so that the alternative reads "the Messiah" (see the book's terms). This applies throughout the passage.

decisions.choice: our leaders (B); the leaders (R)
decisions.reason: "Rulers" can suggest kings. Balanced and Readable say plainly that these are the people in charge in Jerusalem (meaning decision m3).

decisions.choice: el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}
decisions.reason: A title with the article, as at 1:20.

decisions.choice: los gobernantes (L); nuestros dirigentes, los dirigentes (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "gobernantes" can suggest kings; these are the leading men of the council (meaning decision m3). "Miren" is spoken to one another, so it takes the ustedes / vosotros setting.

source.text: ἀλλὰ τοῦτον οἴδαμεν πόθεν ἐστίν· ὁ δὲ χριστὸς ὅταν ἔρχηται οὐδεὶς γινώσκει πόθεν ἐστίν.

records.literal_gloss: But this [one] we know from where he is; but the Christ, whenever he comes, no one knows from where he is."

en.L: But we know where this [man] is from; but the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}}, when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes, no one knows where {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is from."
en.B: But we know where this man comes from. When the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} comes, though, no one will know {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} origin."
en.R: But we know where this man is from. Nobody will know where the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} is from when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} comes."

es.L: Pero este sabemos de dónde es; mas el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, cuando venga, nadie sabe de dónde es».
es.B: Pero nosotros sabemos de dónde viene este hombre. En cambio, cuando venga el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, nadie sabrá de dónde viene».
es.R: Pero sabemos de dónde es este hombre. Cuando venga el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, nadie sabrá de dónde es».

sw.L: Lakini huyu tunajua anakotoka; lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}}, atakapokuja, hakuna anayejua anakotoka."
sw.B: Lakini tunajua mtu huyu anakotoka. Lakini {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atakapokuja, hakuna atakayejua anakotoka."
sw.R: Lakini tunajua mtu huyu anakotoka. Hakuna atakayejua {{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} anakotoka atakapokuja."

decisions.choice: the belief that the Christ would appear without anyone knowing his origin
alternatives: no one will know his family or birthplace
decisions.reason: The speakers hold a view that the Messiah's origin would be hidden until he appeared. It was not the only view: in 7:42 others say he must come from Bethlehem, David's town. Jewish expectation about the Messiah took several forms, and John reports this one as something some in Jerusalem said.

decisions.choice: irony: they know his earthly home, but not where he truly comes from
decisions.reason: They know he is from Nazareth in Galilee (1:45-46; 7:41, 52). John's readers know that he comes from the Father (1:14; 3:13; 6:38), and Jesus says so in 7:28-29. By their own test, the fact that they do not know his true origin fits his being the Christ.

decisions.choice: no one knows: present tense for what will be true when he comes
decisions.reason: The verb is present, "no one knows", stating a rule about the Christ's coming. The sense is that at his appearing no one will know where he is from.

decisions.choice: will know (B, R); origin (B)
decisions.reason: English uses the future after "when he comes"; Literal keeps the present of the Greek (meaning decision m3). Balanced says "origin" to avoid repeating "where ... from".

decisions.choice: sabrá (B, R); sabe (L)
decisions.reason: As in English: Literal keeps the Greek present (meaning decision m3). Spanish needs no pronoun for the coming one ("cuando venga").

source.text: ἔκραξεν οὖν ἐν τῷ ἱερῷ διδάσκων ὁ Ἰησοῦς καὶ λέγων· Κἀμὲ οἴδατε καὶ οἴδατε πόθεν εἰμί· καὶ ἀπ’ ἐμαυτοῦ οὐκ ἐλήλυθα, ἀλλ’ ἔστιν ἀληθινὸς ὁ πέμψας με, ὃν ὑμεῖς οὐκ οἴδατε·

records.literal_gloss: Cried out therefore in the temple teaching the Jesus and saying, "Both me you know, and you know from where I am; and from myself not I have come, but is true the [one] having sent me, whom you not know;

en.L: So Jesus cried out as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching in the temple, saying, "You know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you know where I am from. And I have not come of {{deity_pronoun:myself|Myself}}, but the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is true, whom you do not know.
en.B: So Jesus, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was teaching in the temple courts, cried out, "You know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you know where I come from! Yet I have not come on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. The one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is true, and you do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: While Jesus was teaching in the temple courts, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} called out in a loud voice, "So you know {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you know where I come from! But I did not come on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own. The one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} is real and true. And you do not know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.

es.L: Clamó, pues, Jesús, enseñando en el templo, y dijo: «Me {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} de dónde soy; y no he venido por {{deity_pronoun:mí|Mí}} mismo, pero el que me envió es veraz, a quien {{plural_you:ustedes no conocen|vosotros no conocéis}}.
es.B: Entonces Jesús, mientras enseñaba en los atrios del templo, exclamó: «¡Así que me {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} de dónde vengo! Sin embargo, no he venido por mi cuenta. El que me envió es veraz, y {{plural_you:ustedes no lo conocen|vosotros no lo conocéis}}.
es.R: Mientras Jesús enseñaba en el patio del templo, dijo en voz alta: «¡Así que me {{plural_you:conocen|conocéis}} y {{plural_you:saben|sabéis}} de dónde vengo! Pero yo no vine por mi propia cuenta. El que me envió es real y verdadero. Y {{plural_you:ustedes no lo conocen|vosotros no lo conocéis}}.

sw.L: Basi Yesu alipaza sauti alipokuwa akifundisha hekaluni, akisema, "Mnanijua, na mnajua ninakotoka. Na sikuja kwa nafsi {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}}, lakini yule aliyenituma ni wa kweli, ambaye ninyi hammjui.
sw.B: Basi Yesu, alipokuwa akifundisha katika nyua za hekalu, alipaza sauti, "Mnanijua, na mnajua ninakotoka! Lakini sikuja kwa mamlaka {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Yule aliyenituma ni wa kweli, nanyi hammjui.
sw.R: Yesu alipokuwa akifundisha katika uwanja wa hekalu, alipaza sauti, "Basi mnanijua, na mnajua ninakotoka! Lakini sikuja kwa nia {{deity_pronoun:yangu|Yangu}} {{deity_pronoun:mwenyewe|Mwenyewe}}. Yule aliyenituma ni halisi na wa kweli. Nanyi hammjui.

decisions.choice: cried out: spoke aloud with solemn force
decisions.reason: John uses this verb for a public proclamation, not a shout of anger: John the Baptist cries out his witness (1:15), and Jesus cries out in 7:37 and 12:44. What follows is said for all to hear.

decisions.choice: a statement with irony: you know me and where I am from, so you think
alternatives: a question: do you know me, and do you know where I am from?
a plain statement that they do know his origin
decisions.reason: The words can be read as a plain statement, as a question ("Do you know me, and do you know where I am from?"), or as an ironic statement. Jesus grants what they said in 7:27, that they know where he is from, and then shows how little they know: he did not come on his own, and they do not know the one who sent him. The irony reading fits the turn that follows with "and yet". A question would make the same point less directly.

decisions.choice: true: real and reliable
decisions.reason: The adjective means genuine, the real thing, and also faithful to his word. It is used of God in 17:3, "the only true God". The one who sent Jesus is real and can be trusted, so Jesus is not a self-appointed messenger.

decisions.choice: you do not know him: they do not know God, who sent Jesus
decisions.reason: The speakers worship God in the temple, yet Jesus says they do not know him. John repeats the charge in 8:19 and 8:55; knowing the Father and knowing the one he sent go together (17:3).

decisions.choice: temple courts (B, R)
decisions.reason: The word means the whole temple area, where people gathered and teachers taught, not the sanctuary itself (see the book's terms).

decisions.choice: on {{deity_pronoun:my|My}} own; an exclamation for the irony (B, R); real and true (R)
decisions.reason: "Of myself" is stiff; "on my own" says the same. Balanced and Readable mark the first words as an exclamation to carry the irony (meaning decision m2). Readable adds "real" to show the sense of "true" here.

decisions.choice: ¡Así que ...! (B, R); por mi cuenta
decisions.reason: As in English: Balanced and Readable mark the first words as an exclamation to carry the irony (meaning decision m2), whose footnote gives the other readings.

decisions.choice: los atrios del templo (B); el patio del templo (R)
decisions.reason: The 2:14 choice for the whole temple area.

source.text: ἐγὼ οἶδα αὐτόν, ὅτι παρ’ αὐτοῦ εἰμι κἀκεῖνός με ἀπέστειλεν.

records.literal_gloss: I know him, because from him I am, and that one me sent."

en.L: I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because I am from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and that one sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.B: But I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because I come from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} is the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."
en.R: But I know {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because I came from {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. He is the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

es.L: Yo lo conozco, porque de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} vengo, y aquel me envió».
es.B: Pero yo sí lo conozco, porque vengo de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}} es el que me envió».
es.R: Pero yo sí lo conozco, porque vengo de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Él es el que me envió».

sw.L: {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} namjua, kwa sababu natoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, naye ndiye aliyenituma."
sw.B: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} namjua, kwa sababu natoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}, na {{deity_pronoun:yeye|Yeye}} ndiye aliyenituma."
sw.R: Lakini {{deity_pronoun:mimi|Mimi}} namjua, kwa sababu nilitoka {{deity_pronoun:kwake|Kwake}}. Yeye ndiye aliyenituma."

decisions.choice: I, in contrast to you
decisions.reason: The pronoun "I" is stated for emphasis, set against "you" at the end of 7:28: you do not know him, but I know him.

decisions.choice: I am from him: Jesus comes from God's own presence
decisions.reason: The words answer the question of where he is from (7:27-28). He comes from the Father, as 6:46 and 16:27-28 also say, and only one who is from God has seen him (1:18; 6:46). This is the origin the people do not know.

decisions.choice: and that one sent me: he himself sent me
decisions.reason: The pronoun "that one" points back to God with weight: it is God himself who sent Jesus. Coming from him and being sent by him are the two grounds of Jesus's knowing him.

decisions.choice: But (B, R)
decisions.reason: English shows the emphatic "I" (meaning decision m1) with "but". Readable breaks the verse into two sentences.

decisions.choice: Pero yo sí
decisions.reason: Shows the emphatic "I" (meaning decision m1).

source.text: ἐζήτουν οὖν αὐτὸν πιάσαι, καὶ οὐδεὶς ἐπέβαλεν ἐπ’ αὐτὸν τὴν χεῖρα, ὅτι οὔπω ἐληλύθει ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ.

records.literal_gloss: Were seeking therefore him to seize, and no one laid upon him the hand, because not yet had come the hour of him.

en.L: So they were seeking to seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and no one laid [a] hand on {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hour had not yet come.
en.B: So they tried to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. Yet no one took hold of {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, since {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hour had not yet come.
en.R: Then some people tried to grab {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. But no one touched {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, because {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} time had not come yet.

es.L: Procuraban, pues, prenderlo; pero nadie le echó mano, porque aún no había llegado su hora.
es.B: Entonces trataron de arrestarlo. Pero nadie le puso la mano encima, porque todavía no había llegado su hora.
es.R: Entonces algunos trataron de agarrarlo. Pero nadie lo tocó, porque todavía no había llegado su hora.

sw.L: Basi walikuwa wakitafuta kumkamata, wala hakuna aliyenyosha mkono juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, kwa sababu saa {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa haijafika bado.
sw.B: Basi walijaribu kumkamata. Lakini hakuna aliyemtia mkononi, kwa kuwa saa {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}} ilikuwa haijafika.
sw.R: Ndipo baadhi ya watu walijaribu kumkamata. Lakini hakuna aliyemgusa, kwa sababu wakati {{deity_pronoun:wake|Wake}} ulikuwa haujafika bado.

decisions.choice: they tried: an attempt that did not succeed; the subject is not named
decisions.reason: The tense describes an effort under way. John does not say who "they" were: hostile people in the crowd, or those who spoke for the authorities. In 7:32 the authorities act formally by sending officers.

decisions.choice: laid a hand on him: arrested him
decisions.reason: To lay a hand on someone means to take hold of him by force. The same phrase comes again in 7:44, and 8:20 says the same thing in other words.

decisions.choice: his hour: the appointed time of his death and glorification
decisions.reason: Jesus has said that his hour has not yet come (2:4) and that his time is not yet here (7:6, 8). The hour is the time the Father has set for his death and return to glory (12:23; 13:1; 17:1). Until then no one can seize him; 8:20 says this again.

decisions.choice: took hold of (B); touched, time, some people (R)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say what laying a hand on someone means (meaning decision m2). Readable says "time" for the appointed hour, as the book's terms allow, and "some people" for the unnamed subject (meaning decision m1).

decisions.choice: hora at every level
decisions.reason: As at 2:4: Spanish "su hora" is everyday language for an appointed time, so Readable keeps it; the different word of 7:6-8 is "tiempo".

source.text: ἐκ τοῦ ὄχλου δὲ πολλοὶ ἐπίστευσαν εἰς αὐτόν, καὶ ἔλεγον· Ὁ χριστὸς ὅταν ἔλθῃ μὴ πλείονα σημεῖα ποιήσει ὧν οὗτος ἐποίησεν;

records.literal_gloss: From the crowd but many believed in him, and were saying, "The Christ, whenever he comes, not more signs will he do than [those] which this [one] did?"

en.L: But many from the crowd believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they were saying, "When the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} do more signs than this [man] has done?"
en.B: Many people in the crowd, though, believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and they kept saying, "When the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} comes, {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} will not do more signs than this man has done, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}?"
en.R: But many people in the crowd believed in {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}. They said, "When the {{christos:Christ|Messiah}} comes, will {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} do more signs than this man has done? Surely not!"

es.L: Pero muchos de la multitud creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y decían: «El {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, cuando venga, ¿hará más señales que las que este ha hecho?».
es.B: Sin embargo, muchos de la multitud creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y decían: «Cuando venga el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, ¿acaso hará más señales que las que ha hecho este hombre?».
es.R: Pero muchas personas de la multitud creyeron en {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}. Decían: «Cuando venga el {{christos:Cristo|Mesías}}, ¿hará más señales que este hombre? ¡Seguro que no!».

sw.L: Lakini wengi katika umati walimwamini, wakawa wakisema, "{{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atakapokuja, je, atafanya ishara nyingi kuliko alizofanya huyu?"
sw.B: Hata hivyo watu wengi katika umati walimwamini, wakawa wakisema, "{{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atakapokuja, hatafanya ishara nyingi kuliko alizofanya mtu huyu, sivyo?"
sw.R: Lakini watu wengi katika umati walimwamini. Wakasema, "{{christos:Kristo|Masihi}} atakapokuja, je, atafanya ishara nyingi kuliko alizofanya mtu huyu? Hapana!"

decisions.choice: a question that expects the answer no
decisions.reason: The question opens with the negative that looks for "no": the Christ could hardly do more signs than this man has. The speakers are close to saying that Jesus is the Christ.

decisions.choice: believed in him: a real but early belief
decisions.reason: John uses the same words for true faith (3:16) and for belief that does not yet go deep (2:23-25; 8:30-31). Here belief rests on his signs; it stands against the hostility of 7:30.

decisions.choice: signs: deeds that point to who Jesus is
decisions.reason: John calls Jesus's works signs because they show his glory and lead people to believe (2:11; 20:30-31). In Jerusalem he had healed the man at the pool (5:1-9), and others had seen his signs at the Passover (2:23).

decisions.choice: a tag question (B); an added "Surely not!" (R)
decisions.reason: English shows that a "no" is expected (meaning decision m1) with "will he?" at the end, or with a short reply. Literal keeps a plain question.

decisions.choice: ¿acaso ...? (B); ¡Seguro que no! (R)
decisions.reason: Shows that the question expects "no" (meaning decision m1).

source.text: Ἤκουσαν οἱ Φαρισαῖοι τοῦ ὄχλου γογγύζοντος περὶ αὐτοῦ ταῦτα, καὶ ἀπέστειλαν οἱ ἀρχιερεῖς καὶ οἱ Φαρισαῖοι ὑπηρέτας ἵνα πιάσωσιν αὐτόν.

records.literal_gloss: Heard the Pharisees the crowd muttering about him these things, and sent the chief priests and the Pharisees officers that they might seize him.

en.L: The Pharisees heard the crowd muttering these things about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}, and the chief priests and the Pharisees sent officers to seize {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.B: The Pharisees heard the crowd talking quietly about {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} in this way, so the chief priests and the Pharisees sent temple police to arrest {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}.
en.R: The Pharisees heard what the people in the crowd were saying quietly about Jesus. So the leading priests and the Pharisees sent some temple guards to take {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}} away.

es.L: Oyeron los fariseos a la multitud que murmuraba estas cosas acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, y los principales sacerdotes y los fariseos enviaron alguaciles para prenderlo.
es.B: Los fariseos oyeron que la multitud murmuraba esto acerca de {{deity_pronoun:él|Él}}, así que los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos enviaron a los guardias del templo para arrestarlo.
es.R: Los fariseos oyeron lo que la gente decía en voz baja acerca de Jesús. Entonces los jefes de los sacerdotes y los fariseos enviaron a unos guardias del templo para que se lo llevaran.

sw.L: Mafarisayo waliusikia umati ukinung'unika mambo haya juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, na wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakatuma watumishi wamkamate.
sw.B: Mafarisayo waliusikia umati ukinong'ona hivyo juu {{deity_pronoun:yake|Yake}}, basi wakuu wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakatuma walinzi wa hekalu wamkamate.
sw.R: Mafarisayo walisikia yale watu katika umati waliyokuwa wakinong'ona juu ya Yesu. Basi viongozi wa makuhani na Mafarisayo wakatuma baadhi ya walinzi wa hekalu wamchukue.

decisions.choice: muttering: talking in low voices
decisions.reason: The verb means talk under one's breath. It can mean grumbling, as in 6:41, but here, as in 7:12, it is the crowd's quiet talk about whether Jesus is the Christ. The Pharisees hear the favorable talk of 7:31.

decisions.choice: the chief priests and the Pharisees: the council's leading members
decisions.reason: The chief priests were the high priest and the leading men of the priestly families who ran the temple. Together with the Pharisees among them they made up the Jerusalem council; John names the two groups together in 7:45, 11:47, 11:57 and 18:3.

decisions.choice: officers: the temple police serving the council
decisions.reason: The word means attendants or assistants. Here they are the men who kept order in the temple for the chief priests. They come back empty-handed in 7:45-46, and they arrest Jesus in 18:3, 12.

decisions.choice: temple police (B); temple guards, take him away (R); leading priests (R)
decisions.reason: "Officers" alone does not say whose officers these are. Balanced and Readable name their role (meaning decision m3). Readable says "leading priests" so that "chief" is not taken as a single leader.

decisions.choice: alguaciles (L); guardias del templo (B, R); jefes de los sacerdotes (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: names whose officers these were (meaning decision m3). "Murmurar" covers quiet talk as in 7:12.

source.text: εἶπεν οὖν ὁ Ἰησοῦς· Ἔτι χρόνον μικρὸν μεθ’ ὑμῶν εἰμι καὶ ὑπάγω πρὸς τὸν πέμψαντά με.

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jesus, "Yet time little with you I am, and I go to the [one] having sent me.

en.L: So Jesus said, "Yet a little time I am with you, and [then] I go to the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.B: So Jesus said, "For a little while more I am with you; then I go away to the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.
en.R: Then Jesus said, "I will be here with you just a little longer. Then I will go back to the one who sent {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}.

es.L: Dijo, pues, Jesús: «Todavía un poco de tiempo estoy con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}}, y [luego] voy al que me envió.
es.B: Entonces Jesús dijo: «Estaré con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} un poco más de tiempo; luego me iré al que me envió.
es.R: Entonces Jesús dijo: «Voy a estar aquí con {{plural_you:ustedes|vosotros}} solo un poco más. Después volveré al que me envió.

sw.L: Basi Yesu akasema, "Bado muda mfupi niko pamoja nanyi, [kisha] naenda kwa yule aliyenituma.
sw.B: Basi Yesu akasema, "Kwa muda mfupi zaidi niko pamoja nanyi; kisha naenda zangu kwa yule aliyenituma.
sw.R: Kisha Yesu akasema, "Nitakuwa hapa pamoja nanyi kwa muda mfupi tu. Kisha nitarudi kwa yule aliyenituma.

decisions.choice: a little while: the short time left before his death
decisions.reason: Jesus speaks of the time left before he is taken from them. He says the same to the crowd in 12:35 and to his disciples in 13:33 and 16:16-19. The officers have just been sent to arrest him, but the timing is his, not theirs (7:30).

decisions.choice: I go: I go away, return to the Father
decisions.reason: John uses this verb for Jesus's departure to the Father through his death and resurrection (8:14, 21; 13:3, 33; 16:5). He came from the one who sent him (7:29) and goes back to him.

decisions.choice: then (all levels); go away (B); go back (R)
decisions.reason: The "and" joins two stages: first a little time with them, then his going. English shows the order with "then", bracketed in Literal. Balanced says "go away" for John's word of departure (meaning decision m2); Readable says "go back", since he came from the Father (7:29).

decisions.choice: [luego] (L); luego, después (B, R)
decisions.reason: As in English: shows the two stages (meaning decision m2).

source.text: ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν.

records.literal_gloss: You will seek me and not will find, and where am I you not are able to come."

en.L: You will seek {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and will not find [{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}], and where I am, you cannot come."
en.B: You will search for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and not find {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you cannot come where I am."
en.R: You will look for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you will not find {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You are not able to come where I am."

es.L: Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}} y no me {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}, y donde yo estoy, {{plural_you:ustedes no pueden|vosotros no podéis}} venir».
es.B: Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}} y no me {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}, y adonde yo estoy {{plural_you:ustedes no pueden|vosotros no podéis}} venir».
es.R: Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}}, y no me {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}. {{plural_you:Ustedes no pueden|Vosotros no podéis}} venir adonde yo estoy».

sw.L: Mtanitafuta wala hamtaniona, na mahali nilipo, ninyi hamwezi kuja."
sw.B: Mtanitafuta lakini hamtanipata, wala hamwezi kuja mahali nilipo."
sw.R: Mtanitafuta, lakini hamtanipata. Hamwezi kuja mahali nilipo."

decisions.choice: where I am: the present tense for where he will be with the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus does not say "where I will be" but "where I am". He speaks of the Father's presence as his own place, where he belongs already (1:18; 17:24; also 12:26 and 14:3). The emphatic "I" is set against "you". Some readers also hear in the words his "I am" sayings; here the plain sense of place comes first.

decisions.choice: you will seek me and not find me: when it is too late
decisions.reason: They are seeking him now to kill him (7:1, 25, 30). A time will come when they look for him and he is gone. In 8:21 Jesus adds that they will die in their sin. He says the same words to his disciples in 13:33, but promises to come back for them (14:3).

decisions.choice: a possible echo of Wisdom's warning in Proverbs
decisions.reason: In Proverbs 1:28 Wisdom says that those who rejected her will seek her and not find her. The words are close, and John elsewhere presents Jesus in terms used of God's wisdom, but the passage does not quote Proverbs, and the echo may not be intended.

decisions.choice: search for (B); look for (R)
decisions.reason: "Seek" is less common in speech; Balanced and Readable use everyday words, as at 6:24. They repeat "me", which Literal brackets, and put "where I am" after the verb, the usual English order.

decisions.choice: no me encontrarán, no supplied word
decisions.reason: Spanish needs the object clitic "me" with "encontrar", so Literal needs no bracket.

source.text: εἶπον οὖν οἱ Ἰουδαῖοι πρὸς ἑαυτούς· Ποῦ οὗτος μέλλει πορεύεσθαι ὅτι ἡμεῖς οὐχ εὑρήσομεν αὐτόν;

records.literal_gloss: Said therefore the Jews to themselves, "Where this [one] is about to go, that we not will find him?

en.L: So the Jews said to one another, "Where is this [man] about to go, that we will not find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.B: So the Jewish leaders said to one another, "Where is this man going to go, that we will not find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?
en.R: The Jewish leaders asked each other, "Where is this man planning to go, where we will not be able to find {{deity_pronoun:him|Him}}?

es.L: Dijeron, pues, los judíos entre sí: «¿Adónde se va a ir este, que nosotros no lo encontraremos?
es.B: Entonces los dirigentes judíos se decían unos a otros: «¿Adónde piensa irse este hombre, que no lo vamos a encontrar?
es.R: Los dirigentes judíos se preguntaban unos a otros: «¿Adónde piensa ir este hombre, que no lo podremos encontrar?

sw.L: Basi Wayahudi wakaambiana, "Huyu anakusudia kwenda wapi, hata sisi tusimpate?
sw.B: Basi viongozi wa Wayahudi wakaambiana, "Mtu huyu anakusudia kwenda wapi, hata tusimpate?
sw.R: Viongozi wa Wayahudi wakaulizana, "Mtu huyu anapanga kwenda wapi, mahali ambapo hatutaweza kumpata?

decisions.choice: the Jews: the authorities and those around them who oppose Jesus
alternatives: the listeners in the temple generally
decisions.reason: Jesus has just spoken to the officers sent by the chief priests and the Pharisees (7:32) and to those who seek him (7:34). Those who reply take his words as being about them, the ones who would be searching for him. In this chapter "the Jews" are the authorities who seek to kill him (7:1, 11, 13). They may include people in the temple who sided with them; it is not the people as a whole, since the crowd, the people of Jerusalem and Jesus himself are all Jews.

decisions.choice: they misunderstand: they think of a journey, he means his return to the Father
decisions.reason: Jesus spoke of going to the one who sent him (7:33). His hearers think only of places on a map, where he might go out of their reach. John often lets hearers take Jesus's words on the wrong level (3:4; 4:11; 6:52); 8:22 repeats the misunderstanding in a darker form.

decisions.choice: the Jewish leaders
decisions.reason: Where the word means the authorities, Balanced and Readable name them (see the book's terms). The footnote gives the word John wrote.

decisions.choice: los judíos (L); los dirigentes judíos (B, R)
decisions.reason: Here the word means the authorities and those around them (meaning decision m1), so Balanced and Readable name them. The word John wrote is "los judíos".

source.text: μὴ εἰς τὴν διασπορὰν τῶν Ἑλλήνων μέλλει πορεύεσθαι καὶ διδάσκειν τοὺς Ἕλληνας;

records.literal_gloss: Not to the dispersion of the Greeks he is about to go and to teach the Greeks?

en.L: He is not about to go to the Dispersion among the Greeks and teach the Greeks, is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}}?
en.B: Surely {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does not intend to go to the Jews scattered among the Greeks, and teach the Greeks?
en.R: Is {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} going to go to the Jews who live far away in Greek lands, and teach the Greeks? Surely not!

es.L: ¿Acaso va a ir a la Dispersión entre los griegos y a enseñar a los griegos?
es.B: ¿Acaso piensa ir a los judíos que viven dispersos entre los griegos, y enseñar a los griegos?
es.R: ¿Va a ir a los judíos que viven lejos, en tierras griegas, y enseñar a los griegos? ¡Seguro que no!

sw.L: Je, anakusudia kwenda kwa Wayahudi wa Utawanyiko kati ya Wagiriki, na kuwafundisha Wagiriki?
sw.B: Hakika hakusudii kwenda kwa Wayahudi waliotawanyika kati ya Wagiriki, na kuwafundisha Wagiriki?
sw.R: Je, ataenda kwa Wayahudi wanaoishi mbali katika nchi za Kigiriki, na kuwafundisha Wagiriki? Hapana!

decisions.choice: a scornful question that expects no
decisions.reason: The question begins with the negative that looks for "no". The speakers mock the idea: a teacher of Israel would hardly leave the land to teach foreigners.

decisions.choice: the Dispersion among the Greeks: Jews living outside the land in the Greek-speaking world
decisions.reason: The word means "scattering" and was used for the Jewish communities living outside the land of Israel. "Of the Greeks" says where they were scattered: among the Greek-speaking peoples around the eastern Mediterranean.

decisions.choice: the Greeks: non-Jews, people of Greek language and culture
decisions.reason: "The Greeks" here stands for Gentiles in general, the peoples among whom the Dispersion lived. Some take it to mean Greek-speaking Jews, but the speakers have just named the Jews of the Dispersion; the further step, teaching the Greeks themselves, is the point of the scorn. In 12:20 the word is used of Greeks who came up to worship at the festival.

decisions.choice: irony: what they mock comes true
decisions.reason: The speakers mean the idea as an absurdity, but John's readers know that it happens: Greeks come seeking Jesus as his hour arrives (12:20-23), and he has other sheep to gather (10:16; 11:52). Through his disciples his teaching reached the Greeks.

decisions.choice: the Jews scattered among the Greeks (B); the Jews who live far away in Greek lands (R)
decisions.reason: "The Dispersion" is a technical term most readers will not know. Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m2). Balanced puts the expected "no" into "surely ... not"; Readable adds a short answer.

decisions.choice: los judíos que viven dispersos entre los griegos (B); los judíos que viven lejos, en tierras griegas (R)
decisions.reason: As in English: "la Dispersión" is a technical term; Balanced and Readable say what it means (meaning decision m2).

decisions.choice: Wagiriki
decisions.reason: "Wayunani" is the older Bible word for Greeks; "Wagiriki" is the word readers use today. The meaning note explains that non-Jews of Greek language and culture are meant.

source.text: τίς ἐστιν ὁ λόγος οὗτος ὃν εἶπε· Ζητήσετέ με καὶ οὐχ εὑρήσετέ, καὶ ὅπου εἰμὶ ἐγὼ ὑμεῖς οὐ δύνασθε ἐλθεῖν;

records.literal_gloss: What is the word this which he said, 'You will seek me and not will find, and where am I you not are able to come'?"

en.L: What is this word that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} said, 'You will seek {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and will not find [{{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}], and where I am, you cannot come'?"
en.B: What is this saying of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}}, 'You will search for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} and not find {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you cannot come where I am'?"
en.R: What does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mean when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} says, 'You will look for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, and you will not find {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}. You are not able to come where I am'?"

es.L: ¿Qué es esta palabra que dijo: “Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}} y no me {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}, y donde yo estoy, {{plural_you:ustedes no pueden|vosotros no podéis}} venir”?».
es.B: ¿Qué quiere decir con eso de: “Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}} y no me {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}, y adonde yo estoy {{plural_you:ustedes no pueden|vosotros no podéis}} venir”?».
es.R: ¿Qué quiere decir cuando dice: “Me {{plural_you:buscarán|buscaréis}}, y no me {{plural_you:encontrarán|encontraréis}}. {{plural_you:Ustedes no pueden|Vosotros no podéis}} venir adonde yo estoy”?».

sw.L: Ni neno gani hili alilolisema, 'Mtanitafuta wala hamtaniona, na mahali nilipo, ninyi hamwezi kuja'?"
sw.B: Maneno haya aliyoyasema yanamaanisha nini, 'Mtanitafuta lakini hamtanipata, wala hamwezi kuja mahali nilipo'?"
sw.R: Anamaanisha nini anaposema, 'Mtanitafuta, lakini hamtanipata. Hamwezi kuja mahali nilipo'?"

decisions.choice: word: saying; they ask what it means
decisions.reason: "What is this word" asks about the meaning of what Jesus said. The speakers repeat his words exactly as 7:34 has them, which shows they heard him clearly but cannot make sense of them.

decisions.choice: the repetition stresses their failure to understand
decisions.reason: John repeats the whole saying so the reader sees its weight. The question is left without an answer; the reader knows that he goes to the Father (7:33). Even the disciples later ask a similar question (16:17-18).

decisions.choice: What is this saying of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} (B); What does {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} mean (R)
decisions.reason: The Greek asks what this word is. Balanced calls it a saying; Readable asks what he means. Both repeat the words exactly as each level gave them in 7:34.

decisions.choice: the saying repeated exactly as in 7:34
decisions.reason: As in English: every level repeats Jesus's words exactly, so the reader sees their weight (meaning decision m2).
